question:
An 81-year-old man is admitted to the hospital due to acute decompensated heart failure. He has type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, coronary artery disease, and congestive heart failure. Current medications include lisinopril, metformin, and low-dose aspirin. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 45 years. His temperature is 37.6°C (99.7°F), pulse is 105/min and regular, respirations are 21/min, and blood pressure is 103/64 mm Hg. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 13.7 g/dL
Leukocyte count 8200/mm3
Serum
Na+ 128 mEq/L
Cl- 98 mEq/L
K+ 4.9 mEq/L
Urea nitrogen 58 mg/dL
Glucose 200 mg/dL
Creatinine 2.2 mg/dL
Which of the following changes in the medication regimen is most appropriate in this patient at this time?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Type 2 diabetes mellitus" -> "Metformin therapy" -> "Decreased blood glucose levels" -> "Improved glycemic control" -> "Reduced risk of diabetic complications" -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: "Heart failure" -> "Lisinopril therapy" -> "Improved cardiac function" -> "Reduced blood pressure" -> "Decreased workload on the heart" -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: "Congestive heart failure" -> "Low-dose aspirin therapy" -> "Reduced risk of thrombotic events" -> 75% confidence. CHAIN: "Hypertension" -> "Lisinopril therapy" -> "Vasodilation" -> "Lowered blood pressure" -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: "Chronic smoking history" -> "Increased risk of cardiovascular disease" -> "Potential exacerbation of heart failure" -> 70% confidence. CHAIN: "High glucose levels" -> "Metformin therapy" -> "Improved insulin sensitivity" -> "Lowered blood glucose levels" -> 80%
enhanced_information: Discontinuing metformin therapy may be most appropriate in this patient at this time due to his acute decompensated heart failure and elevated creatinine levels, which can increase the risk of lactic acidosis with metformin use. The chain linking metformin therapy to improved glycemic control and reduced risk of diabetic complications is relevant but should be weighed against the patient's current clinical status.
analysis: In this case, the most appropriate change in the medication regimen is to discontinue metformin therapy. The patient's elevated creatinine levels and acute decompensated heart failure increase the risk of lactic acidosis with metformin use. While metformin is beneficial for glycemic control, the potential harm outweighs the benefits in this clinical scenario.
